problem: 'Columns may stack at half width' is not what happens. Outside a row the flex properties are ignored (Bootstrap 5 keeps each column at one-third width, Bootstrap 4 falls back to full width) and the gutter padding is gone, so the columns simply stop behaving as a grid row. 'Half width' is invented and will confuse a student who tries it.
fix: Say instead: without the row there is no flex container and no negative margins, so the gutter padding disappears and the columns no longer line up beside each other as intended.

problem: The formula defines W as the row content width, but the example substitutes 960 px, which is the container content width. A real row is wider than the container content box by the two negative margins, and every column also carries half-gutter padding, so the true box widths are not exactly 320/640/960 px.
fix: Add one line: these widths ignore the gutter; treat them as the share of the 960 px row taken by each column. Use W = 960 px as the row width, or say plainly that the calculation assumes a gutter-less grid.
